title: Environment Map Reflections with Roughness
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that demonstrates environment map reflections with varying roughness on multiple spheres. The scene must be fully interactive with keyboard, mouse, and DOM controls.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 2, 10), looking at origin, FOV 50.
- Create a dark background (0x111111). Add subtle ambient light (0x404040) and one directional light (white, intensity 1.0) at position (5, 10, 7).
- Generate a procedural HDR-style environment map using THREE.PMREMGenerator with a simple gradient scene (use a small scene with colored meshes or a DataTexture to simulate an environment: top half sky-blue 0x87CEEB, bottom half ground-green 0x3a5f0b, with a bright yellow-white sun spot). Apply this as scene.environment.
- Create exactly 7 spheres (SphereGeometry radius 0.8, 64 segments) arranged in a horizontal row from x=-6 to x=6 (evenly spaced). Each sphere uses MeshStandardMaterial with metalness=1.0 and roughness values: [0.0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.45, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0] from left to right.
- All spheres should have the environment map applied via material.envMap (from PMREMGenerator) and envMapIntensity = 1.0.
- Add a ground plane (PlaneGeometry 20x20) at y=-1.5, rotated to be horizontal, with MeshStandardMaterial color 0x333333, roughness 0.9, metalness 0.1.

## Selectable Sphere System
- Implement raycasting on click to select a sphere. The selected sphere gets a visible outline (use a slightly larger wireframe sphere overlay, or change emissive to 0x333333). Only one sphere can be selected at a time.
- Track the currently selected sphere index (0-6, or -1 if none).

## Interactive Controls
- DOM slider (id='roughnessSlider', range 0.0 to 1.0, step 0.01) that adjusts the roughness of the SELECTED sphere. Label it with current value (id='roughnessValue'). Disabled when no sphere is selected.
- DOM slider (id='metalnessSlider', range 0.0 to 1.0, step 0.01) that adjusts the metalness of the SELECTED sphere. Label with value (id='metalnessValue'). Disabled when no sphere is selected.
- DOM slider (id='envIntensitySlider', range 0.0 to 3.0, step 0.1) that adjusts envMapIntensity for ALL spheres globally. Label with value (id='envIntensityValue'). Default 1.0.
- DOM button (id='resetBtn') that resets ALL spheres to their original roughness values [0.0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.45, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0], metalness=1.0, envMapIntensity=1.0, and deselects any sphere.
- DOM button (id='undoBtn') that undoes the last material property change (maintain a history stack of at least 20 entries). Each slider change that is committed (on 'input' event) pushes to history.
- Keyboard 'R' key: toggle between metalness=1.0 and metalness=0.0 for the selected sphere (acts as a quick metal/dielectric toggle). Push to undo history.
- Keyboard 'Tab' key: cycle selection to the next sphere (wrap around from 6 to 0). Prevent default tab behavior.
- Keyboard 'Escape' key: deselect current sphere.
- Keyboard '1'-'7' keys: directly select sphere at index 0-6.

## Color Mode
- DOM dropdown (id='colorMode', options: 'white' (default, color 0xffffff), 'gold' (0xFFD700), 'copper' (0xB87333), 'chrome' (0xCCCCCC)). Changing this sets the base color of ALL spheres to the chosen color. Push to undo history.

## HUD
- Display a HUD overlay (id='hud') in top-left showing: selected sphere index (or 'None'), its current roughness, metalness, envMapIntensity, and the current color mode name.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - sphereCount: number (always 7)
  - selectedIndex: number (-1 if none)
  - spheres: array of 7 objects each with { roughness: number, metalness: number, envMapIntensity: number, colorHex: string (like '#ffffff'), positionX: number }
  - globalEnvIntensity: number
  - colorMode: string ('white'|'gold'|'copper'|'chrome')
  - undoStackSize: number
  - cameraZ: number
  - envMapApplied: boolean (true if environment map is set on scene)
  - groundPlaneExists: boolean
  - frameCount: number (incremented each frame)

Place all UI controls in a panel (id='controlPanel') positioned at top-right with semi-transparent dark background. Style all sliders and buttons for visibility.
physics_constraints: Roughness must be clamped [0.0, 1.0]. Metalness must be clamped [0.0, 1.0]. envMapIntensity must be clamped [0.0, 3.0]. All material values must be valid floats (no NaN, no Infinity). Undo must restore exact previous values. Reset must restore exact original values. Sphere positions must remain constant throughout all interactions.
